paper_metadata.title: A Study of the Hot Salt Corrosion Behavior of Three Nickel-Based Single-Crystal Superalloys at 900 °C

evidence.quote: A study of the hot salt corrosion behavior of three nickel-based single-crystal superalloys at 900 ◦C was conducted.
The three single-crystal superalloys were obtained through directional solidification to ensure the crystals grow uniformly and continuously, minimizing the formation of grain boundaries and defects
Three alloy bars underwent standard heat treatment to prepare the specimens for analysis, followed by machining into a Φ10 × 170 mm substrate.

mechanisms.name: metal oxidation with cation and cation vacancy migration

evidence.quote: the corrosion mechanism of the three alloys at 900 °C essentially involves the oxidation process of metals, characterized by the migration of metal cations and cation vacancies

mechanisms.name: molten salt decomposition into SO42- and Cl- ions

evidence.quote: Given that the melting points of Na2SO4 and NaCl molten salt media are below 900 °C, they decompose into SO42− and Cl- ions.

mechanisms.name: preferential oxidation of Al, Mo, and Cr

evidence.quote: These O2− molecules preferentially react with Al, Mo, and Cr to form oxides, followed by reactions with Ni and Ti

mechanisms.name: NiO formation compromising protective oxide layer

evidence.quote: While the reaction of Ni with the molten salt may facilitate the formation of an Al2O3 layer, the loose and easily exfoliating nature of NiO reaction products can compromise their protective role, potentially accelerating the degree of melted salt corrosion

mechanisms.name: internal diffusion of S and O along void channels

evidence.quote: S and O atoms continue to penetrate along these channels, corroding deeper into the material.
Ta preferentially forms Ta2O5 oxides during oxidation, which subsequently react with the corrosive media to ultimately exist as stable solid
